framework.name: next
framework.notes: App Router at repo root (app/, lib/, components/ - no src/ dir). next.config.js sets output:'standalone', reactStrictMode, images.domains for google/github avatars, experimental.serverActions.allowedOrigins ['localhost:3000'], and wraps the config with withSentryConfig.

monorepo.notes: Single package.json at root, no workspaces field; .npmrc sets engine-strict=true

auth.notes: NextAuth v4 (^4.24.5) + @next-auth/prisma-adapter, session strategy 'database'. Providers: Google and GitHub only - no credentials/email-password or magic-link path and no /api/auth/register route. User.role defaults to 'user' in prisma/schema.prisma and app/dashboard/admin/page.tsx gates on session.user.role === 'admin', but the session callback in lib/auth.ts only copies id + stripe fields (types/next-auth.d.ts does not declare role), so /dashboard/admin redirects for every user.

flags: ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS / ENABLE_ANALYTICS / ENABLE_FEEDBACK documented in .env.example but never read

env.notes: Names only, never values. Count is the union of .env.example (32 names) plus names the code reads that the example omits (STRIPE_PRICE_ID_BASIC_YEARLY, STRIPE_PRICE_ID_PRO_YEARLY, STRIPE_PRICE_ID_ENTERPRISE_YEARLY, NODE_ENV, CI). 12 documented names are read by nothing (STRIPE_PUBLIC_KEY, REDIS_PASSWORD, ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS/ANALYTICS/FEEDBACK, PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH, MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS, LOCKOUT_DURATION_MINUTES, COOKIE_CONSENT_VERSION, TERMS_VERSION, PRIVACY_VERSION; NEXTAUTH_URL is consumed by next-auth itself). required_at_build reflects the env the CI 'build' job passes; next.config.js additionally reads SENTRY_ORG/SENTRY_PROJECT at config load.

deploy.notes: 3-stage node:18-alpine Dockerfile (deps -> builder -> runner, USER nextjs, CMD node server.js) using `npm ci` + `npx prisma generate`; docker-compose.yml adds postgres:15-alpine plus the app on port 3000. vercel.json overrides buildCommand to `prisma generate && next build` and installCommand to `npm install`. No lockfile is committed, so `npm ci` in both Docker and CI fails; the Dockerfile also COPYs /app/public, which does not exist in the repo. No prisma/migrations directory and db:migrate is `prisma migrate dev` (interactive, dev-only) - there is no deploy-safe migration command.

tests.notes: CI has 4 jobs (lint, test, e2e, build), each starting with `npm ci`. The test job runs `jest --ci` against a repo with zero unit/integration test files (only jest.config.js + jest.setup.js exist). Playwright's single spec e2e/example.spec.ts holds 3 smoke tests whose expected headings match the current pages; playwright.config.ts runs chromium/firefox/webkit with a `npm run dev` webServer. README's `npm test` maps to `jest --watch`.

pitfalls.detail: npm install cannot resolve at all: dependency '@radix-ui/react-skeleton@^0.0.5' does not exist on npm (registry 404; Radix ships no skeleton primitive) - a fresh install fails before anything else can be tried

No lockfile is committed (no package-lock.json/yarn.lock/pnpm-lock.yaml) yet CI and the Dockerfile both run `npm ci`, which requires one -> all four CI jobs and the docker build die at the install step

README claims '75+ enterprise features', '18,000+ lines of production code', '150+ files' and 'Zero technical debt'; measured: 102 files, 8,006 lines of .ts/.tsx/.js, 12 pages, 14 API routes, 26 Prisma models, and the badges point at github.com/your-repo with 'View Demo' as a dead '#' anchor
pitfalls.evidence: README.md vs git tree + per-file line counts

pitfalls.detail: 13 of ~26 lib modules are imported by no route, page or component (api-docs, two-factor, jobs, rate-limit, security, audit, compliance, feature-flags, onboarding, referrals, impersonation, usage-tracking, analytics-advanced) - 2FA, background jobs, referrals, feature flags, the Swagger playground and audit logging exist as code but are unreachable
pitfalls.evidence: import sweep over every .ts/.tsx/.js file vs app/api route list

pitfalls.detail: /dashboard/admin can never be reached: the page redirects unless session.user.role === 'admin', but the session callback in lib/auth.ts never copies role onto the session and types/next-auth.d.ts does not declare it, so every user is bounced back to /dashboard

About a dozen declared dependencies are never imported anywhere: framer-motion, recharts, react-chartjs-2, zustand, next-themes, sonner, react-hook-form, zod, date-fns, cookie, @stripe/stripe-js, swagger-ui-react, plus radix primitives checkbox/popover/progress/select/separator/switch - install weight and audit noise with no feature behind them

Dockerfile does `COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public` but the repo has no public/ directory, so the image build fails; node:18-alpine also installs only libc6-compat while bcrypt is a native addon

No prisma/migrations directory is committed and db:migrate is `prisma migrate dev` (interactive, dev-only), so there is no deploy-safe migration path; the README quick-start uses db:push, and db:seed points at prisma/seed.ts which does not exist
pitfalls.evidence: package.json scripts; git tree; prisma/schema.prisma; README.md

pitfalls.detail: npm install runs postinstall `prisma generate` and prepare `husky install` (the latter fails outside a git checkout), and .npmrc sets engine-strict=true so Node < 18 aborts the install outright

.env.example documents 12 names the code never reads (STRIPE_PUBLIC_KEY, REDIS_PASSWORD, ENABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS/ANALYTICS/FEEDBACK, PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH, MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS, LOCKOUT_DURATION_MINUTES, COOKIE_CONSENT_VERSION, TERMS_VERSION, PRIVACY_VERSION, NEXTAUTH_URL) while the code reads 3 STRIPE_PRICE_ID_*_YEARLY names that are not documented, so yearly checkout sends an undefined priceId; security policy values are hardcoded in lib/security.ts instead of read from env

The CI build job passes only DATABASE_URL/NEXTAUTH_SECRET/NEXTAUTH_URL, next.config.js reads SENTRY_ORG/SENTRY_PROJECT at config load, and lib/stripe.ts constructs Stripe from a non-null-asserted STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (likewise lib/email.ts with RESEND_API_KEY) - any import of those modules without env throws at module scope

lib/jobs.ts opens an ioredis connection and instantiates four BullMQ queues at module scope, so merely importing the existing queueEmail helper requires a reachable Redis (default localhost:6379) at runtime or build

verdict.best_for: A read-only reference/demo artifact - e.g. harvesting a broad multi-tenant Prisma schema or shadcn-style dashboard pages for ideas - not a base to install and launch.
verdict.weak_for: Any real launch as-is: install is impossible (phantom @radix-ui/react-skeleton), there is no lockfile, no migrations, zero unit tests, sign-in is Google/GitHub OAuth only, and roughly half the advertised features are unreferenced lib code.
verdict.swap_burden: heavy - Stripe, Resend, Redis/BullMQ, Sentry and NextAuth all need touching, but first the dependency tree, lockfile, migrations and ~13 dead modules have to be fixed or triaged.
